{{nihongo|'''Kuwada Shrine'''|桑田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tanba Province]].

== Japanese content ==
{{Coordinates list}}
'''Kuwada Shrine''' (くわだじんじゃ / くわたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} listed in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}'' for Kuwata District, {{ill|Tanba Province|cs|Tanba (provincie)|de|Provinz Tamba|es|Provincia de Tanba|fa|ولایت تانبا|fr|Province de Tanba|gl|Provincia de Tanba|id|Provinsi Tamba|it|Tanba (provincia)|ja|丹波国|ko|단바국|lt|Tambos žemė|nl|Tamba (provincie)|pt|Província de Tanba|ru|Тамба (провинция)|simple|Tamba Province|sk|Tanba (provincia)|sr|Провинција Тамба|tr|Tamba (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тамба|zh|丹波國|zh_min_nan|Tanba-kok|qid=Q954511}}. The following two shrines are treated as candidate shrines ({{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}}):

* 1. {{ill|Kuwada Shrine|ja|桑田神社|qid=Q11537594|lt=Kuwada Shrine}} (Shinocho Yamamoto, {{ill|Kameoka, Kyoto|ar|كاميوكا|azb|کامه‌اوکا، کیوتو|ce|Камеока|ceb|Kameoka-shi|cs|Kameoka|de|Kameoka|eo|Kameoka|es|Kameoka (Kioto)|eu|Kameoka (Kyoto)|fa|کامه‌اوکا، کیوتو|fi|Kameoka|fr|Kameoka|gl|Kameoka|id|Kameoka, Kyōto|it|Kameoka|ja|亀岡市|ko|가메오카시|lt|Kameoka|mg|Kameoka|my|ခမဲအိုခမြို့၊ ကျိုတို|mzn|کامه‌اوکا، کیوتو|nl|Kameoka|pl|Kameoka|pt|Kameoka|ro|Kameoka|ru|Камеока|simple|Kameoka, Kyoto|sv|Kameoka|tg|Камеока|th|คาเมโอกะ|tl|Kameoka, Kyoto|tr|Kameoka|tt|Камеока|uk|Камеока|ur|کامی اوکا، کیوٹو|vi|Kameoka, Kyōto|war|Kameoka, Kyoto|zh|龜岡市|zh_classical|龜岡市|zh_min_nan|Kameoka-chhī|zh_yue|龜岡|qid=Q633996}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}) - former {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}
* 2. {{ill|Kuwada Shrine|ja|桑田神社|qid=Q11537594|lt=Kuwada Shrine}} (Shinocho Umahori, Kameoka, Kyoto) - former {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=mukakusha}}

=== Overview ===
The ''Engishiki Jinmyocho'' records "Kuwada Shrine, Kuwata District, Tanba Province." Two candidate shrines survive in Kameoka City. The Umahori shrine is sometimes said to be the former original site of the Yamamoto shrine, but the exact history is unclear.

Both are in eastern Kameoka near the entrance to {{ill|Hozu Gorge|ja|保津峡|zh|保津峽|qid=Q10887680}} on the right bank of the Oi River; {{ill|Uketa Shrine|ja|請田神社|qid=Q11631810}} stands across the river.

'''Kuwada Shrine''' in Yamamoto is a Shinto shrine in Kameoka, Kyoto. It is a candidate Engishiki shrine; its former rank was village shrine.

=== Enshrined deities ===
; Main deity
* {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|fr|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|Ichikishima-hime|zh|市寸島比賣命|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}}
; Additional deities
* {{ill|Oyamakui no Kami|Q10935105|qid=Q10935105|lt=Oyamakui-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|Q386563|qid=Q386563|lt=Oyamazumi-no-Mikoto}}

=== History ===
Tradition says the deities, together with those of {{ill|Kuwayama Shrine|ja|鍬山神社|zh|鍬山神社|qid=Q11650775}}, opened a channel through Hozukyo to reclaim the former lake area of the {{ill|Kameoka Basin|Q11181997|qid=Q11181997}}. The site at the basin entrance was politically important, and the Hata clan is said to have advanced here early.<ref name=setsumei/> Shrine tradition also links the old place-name "Tanba" to "Taniba."<ref name=kameoka>''Kameoka Shrine Gazetteer'', Kuwada Shrine section.</ref>

The shrine buildings burned in the Tenmei era (1781-1789).<ref name=chosayama/> Until 1873, it reportedly shared the name "Uketa Shrine (Ukita Shrine)" with the shrine across the river.<ref name=setsumei>On-site explanatory board.</ref> It was ranked village shrine in June 1873 and officially used the name "Kuwada Shrine" in June 1877.<ref name=chosayama/>

'''Kuwada Shrine''' in Umahori is the second candidate shrine. Its former rank was mukakusha.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|fr|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|Ichikishima-hime|zh|市寸島比賣命|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}}

=== History ===
Its history is unclear. A tradition says the deity was moved from this site to the Yamamoto site.<ref name=chosa/>
